As Cuba heads into another month of blackouts due to the near-total fuel blockade imposed by the US, many say their lives now revolve around these power outages. For Ana Rosa Romero, a 70-year-old widow living in a high-rise building, the constant power cuts have transformed her daily life. BBC's Will Grant spoke to her about the impact of the blackouts. The DOJ charged the former leader of Cuba with murder and other crimes for his alleged role in the downing of two civilian aircraft in 1996. BBC correspondent Will Grant reports from Havana, hours after the US charged former Cuban leader with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes. The US government has charged the former Cuban president with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes over the downing of the two planes.

On Wednesday evening, Associated Press journalists saw residents in numerous neighborhoods banging pots and pans and setting fire to trash cans to protest the blackouts. Hours later, Energy and Mines Minister Vicente de la O Levy appeared on Cuban television to describe the energy situation as “critical.” Cuba’s power grid is crumbling, but the government also has blamed the outages on U.S. sanctions after President Donald Trump in January warned of tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba. The Trump administration has demanded that Cuba release political prisoners and move toward political and economic liberalization in return for a lifting of sanctions. The blackouts have led to reduced work hours and food spoilage as refrigerators stop working. In some cases, hospitals have canceled surgeries. HAVANA (AP) — Cuba’s national energy grid suffered a major failure early Thursday that severed power to the island’s eastern provinces, authorities said, as residents in the capital Havana faced ongoing blackouts. Cuba’s aging power grid has eroded in recent years as it faces a prolonged economic crisis, recently made worse by a U.S. energy blockade of the island, where daily life can be an ordeal for many of the country’s 10 million people. The state-run Electric Union said the collapse had stripped power from all eastern provinces from Guantánamo to Ciego de Ávila, and that crews were working to restore power, but it did not give an estimate for how long it would take.

HAVANA (AP) — Cuba’s national energy grid suffered a major failure early Thursday that severed power to the island’s eastern provinces, authorities said, as residents in the capital Havana faced ongoing blackouts.

Cuba’s aging power grid has eroded in recent years as it faces a prolonged economic crisis, recently made worse by a U.S. energy blockade of the island, where daily life can be an ordeal for many of the country’s 10 million people.

The state-run Electric Union said the collapse had stripped power from all eastern provinces from Guantánamo to Ciego de Ávila, and that crews were working to restore power, but it did not give an estimate for how long it would take.

The previous day, Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel had described the energy situation as “tense” after supplies of oil delivered by a Russian vessel in late March ran out. Cuba produces barely 40% of the fuel it needs to power its economy.

Russia announced plans to send a second fuel ship to Cuba in early April. According to Russian news reports, the oil tanker left the Russian Baltic port of Vysotsk in January, but has been stuck in the same place in the Atlantic Ocean for the last several weeks.

Power outages in Havana, where authorities have been rationing power, stretched to 24 consecutive hours on Thursday.

On Wednesday evening, Associated Press journalists saw residents in numerous neighborhoods banging pots and pans and setting fire to trash cans to protest the blackouts. Hours later, Energy and Mines Minister Vicente de la O Levy appeared on Cuban television to describe the energy situation as “critical.”

Cuba’s power grid is crumbling, but the government also has blamed the outages on U.S. sanctions after President Donald Trump in January warned of tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba. The Trump administration has demanded that Cuba release political prisoners and move toward political and economic liberalization in return for a lifting of sanctions.

The blackouts have led to reduced work hours and food spoilage as refrigerators stop working. In some cases, hospitals have canceled surgeries.

Follow AP’s coverage of Latin America and the Caribbean at https://apnews.com/hub/latin-america

payload.title: Kuuban sähkökatkot pitävät kerrostaloasukkaat jatkuvassa epävarmuudessa
payload.summary: Kuuban pitkittyneet sähkökatkot vaikeuttavat arkea erityisesti korkeissa taloissa, joissa hissit pysähtyvät katkojen aikana. Havannassa 70-vuotias leski kertoo, kuinka sähkökatko esti häntä ja hänen miestään poistumasta rakennuksesta tilanteessa, jossa mies olisi tarvinnut hoitoa.
payload.content:
Kuuban toistuvat sähkökatkot ovat tehneet arjesta epävarmaa etenkin kerrostaloissa asuville ihmisille, kun hissit, jääkaapit ja monet välttämättömät palvelut riippuvat sähköstä. Havannassa asuva 70-vuotias Ana Rosa Romero kertoo, että sähkökatkojen vaikutus konkretisoitui raskaasti, kun hänen miehensä tarvitsi lääkärinhoitoa mutta hissi ei toiminut.

## Hissin pysähtyminen voi sulkea asukkaan kotiin

Romero asuu korkeassa asuinrakennuksessa, jossa sähkökatko merkitsee myös hissin pysähtymistä. Hänen mukaansa katkojen vuoksi hän ja hänen miehensä jäivät käytännössä loukkuun tilanteessa, jossa miehen olisi pitänyt päästä hoitoon. Tapaus kuvaa laajempaa ongelmaa: sähkökatkot eivät ole vain epämukavuus, vaan ne voivat estää liikkumisen, hoitoon hakeutumisen ja tavallisten päivittäisten asioiden hoitamisen.

Monille kuubalaisille elämä rytmittyy nyt sähkökatkojen mukaan. Katkot vaikuttavat ruoan säilyttämiseen, työntekoon ja palveluihin. Kun jääkaapit lakkaavat toimimasta, ruoka voi pilaantua. Joissakin tapauksissa sairaalat ovat joutuneet perumaan leikkauksia, mikä kertoo kriisin ulottumisesta myös terveydenhuoltoon.

## Sähköverkon ongelmat ovat syventyneet

Kuuban sähköverkko on heikentynyt vuosien ajan talouskriisin keskellä. Viranomaisten mukaan maan kansallinen sähköverkko kärsi torstain vastaisena yönä vakavasta häiriöstä, joka katkaisi sähköt itäisistä maakunnista Guantánamosta Ciego de Ávilaan. Samaan aikaan myös Havannassa on koettu jatkuvia sähkökatkoja.

Kuuban valtiollinen sähköyhtiö ilmoitti korjaustöiden olevan käynnissä, mutta ei antanut arviota siitä, milloin sähköt saataisiin palautettua. Energiasta vastaava ministeri Vicente de la O Levy kuvasi tilannetta televisiossa kriittiseksi.

## Protesteja ja kasvavaa turhautumista

Sähkökatkot ovat herättäneet myös julkista turhautumista. Keskiviikkoiltana useilla asuinalueilla ihmiset osoittivat mieltään hakkaamalla kattiloita ja pannuja sekä sytyttämällä roskia tuleen. Hallitus on yhdistänyt ongelmia muun muassa Yhdysvaltain pakotteisiin ja energiasaarron vaikutuksiin, mutta arjen seuraukset näkyvät ennen kaikkea kotitalouksissa, sairaaloissa ja työpaikoilla.

Romero kertoo tilanteesta yhden asukkaan näkökulmasta, mutta hänen kokemuksensa tiivistää sen, miksi sähkökatkoista on tullut Kuubassa jatkuvaa epävarmuutta aiheuttava kriisi.

Havannalainen 70-vuotias Ana Rosa Romero kertoo jääneensä miehensä kanssa loukkuun, kun tämä tarvitsi hoitoa.
Viranomaiset ovat kuvanneet maan energiatilannetta kriittiseksi, ja sähkökatkot ovat johtaneet myös protesteihin.

article.source_text:
Will Grant spoke to a 70-year-old widow who says the inability to use her building's elevator during a power outage trapped her and her husband when he needed medical care.

As Cuba heads into another month of blackouts due to the near-total fuel blockade imposed by the US, many say their lives now revolve around these power outages. For Ana Rosa Romero, a 70-year-old widow living in a high-rise building, the constant power cuts have transformed her daily life. BBC's Will Grant spoke to her about the impact of the blackouts. The DOJ charged the former leader of Cuba with murder and other crimes for his alleged role in the downing of two civilian aircraft in 1996. BBC correspondent Will Grant reports from Havana, hours after the US charged former Cuban leader with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes. The US government has charged the former Cuban president with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes over the downing of the two planes.

On Wednesday evening, Associated Press journalists saw residents in numerous neighborhoods banging pots and pans and setting fire to trash cans to protest the blackouts. Hours later, Energy and Mines Minister Vicente de la O Levy appeared on Cuban television to describe the energy situation as “critical.” Cuba’s power grid is crumbling, but the government also has blamed the outages on U.S. sanctions after President Donald Trump in January warned of tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to Cuba. The Trump administration has demanded that Cuba release political prisoners and move toward political and economic liberalization in return for a lifting of sanctions. The blackouts have led to reduced work hours and food spoilage as refrigerators stop working. In some cases, hospitals have canceled surgeries. Follow AP’s coverage of Latin America and the Caribbean at https://apnews.com/hub/latin-america ---

HAVANA (AP) — Cuba’s national energy grid suffered a major failure early Thursday that severed power to the island’s eastern provinces, authorities said, as residents in the capital Havana faced ongoing blackouts. Cuba’s aging power grid has eroded in recent years as it faces a prolonged economic crisis, recently made worse by a U.S. energy blockade of the island, where daily life can be an ordeal for many of the country’s 10 million people. The state-run Electric Union said the collapse had stripped power from all eastern provinces from Guantánamo to Ciego de Ávila, and that crews were working to restore power, but it did not give an estimate for how long it would take.
